2609.28022.title: PISCES: Physics-Informed Solar-wind Convolutional autoEncoder for Space-weather Anomaly Detection and Early Warning
2609.28022.paper_summary: Space weather early warning depends on detecting solar wind transients in in-situ measurements at the first Sun-Earth Lagrange point (L1), before they reach Earth. Fixed thresholds can miss combined magnetic and plasma structure, and many learning methods provide a single anomaly score. We present the Physics-Informed Solar-wind Convolutional autoEncoder for Space-weather (PISCES), a convolutional autoencoder trained without catalog labels on OMNI solar wind measurements under physics constraints. Its loss includes magnetic field consistency, an empirical relation between temperature and velocity, the Parker spiral angle, and penalties on changes between consecutive one-minute samples in derived quantities calculated from the reconstruction. At inference, PISCES separates the anomaly score into magnetic and plasma reconstruction errors, physics relations, and residual corrections, and reports the magnitude of each contribution. Attenuation of the skip connections, selected on validation data, improves average precision for the trained models, while the untrained scores remain nearly the same. The trained models also give a more consistent ordering of these physical contributions. After smoothing with a trailing median, the alarms can precede independently observed sudden commencements, including positive sudden impulses.
2609.28022.paper_summary_zh: 太空天氣的提前預警依賴於在第一個日地拉格朗日點 (L1) 的現場測量中檢測太陽風瞬變，這些瞬變必須在它們到達地球之前被發現。固定的閾值可能會錯過結合的磁場和等離子體結構，許多學習方法提供單一的異常分數。我們提出了物理知識驅動的太陽風卷積自編碼器 (PISCES)，這是一種在物理約束下，基於OMNI太陽風測量訓練的無目錄標籤的卷積自編碼器。它的損失包括磁場一致性、溫度和速度之間的經驗關係、帕克螺旋角，以及對從重建計算出的連續一分鐘樣本之間變化的懲罰。在推斷時，PISCES將異常分數分解為磁場和等離子體重建誤差、物理關係和殘差修正，並報告每個貢獻的大小。基於驗證數據選擇的跳過連接的衰減改善了訓練模型的平均精度，而未訓練的分數幾乎保持不變。訓練模型還提供了這些物理貢獻的更一致排序。在用滯後中位數平滑後，警報可以在獨立觀察到的突然開始之前發出，包括正的突然脈衝。
2609.28022.author: Kevin Lee et.al.
